q: Where does your business data actually live?

opts.t: A main system plus a few spreadsheets

opp.text: Pull your scattered spreadsheets into one connected system, so data is entered once and shared everywhere.
Replace disconnected spreadsheets with one source of truth — no more conflicting versions or manual consolidation.
Move off paper and memory entirely onto a single system your whole team works from.

q: Can you see what you’re actually making — per job, per client, per product — right now?

opts.t: Yes — I can see margins live

opp.text: See true profit per job, client, and product in real time — so you stop guessing which work actually makes money.

opts.t: Only the overall picture, not the detail

opp.text: Break down profitability by job, client, and product instead of one blended number that hides your best and worst work.

opts.t: Not really — I find out at year-end

opp.text: Get live margin visibility instead of discovering profit (or loss) months later when nothing can be changed.

q: How much does your team re-enter the same information by hand?

opp.text: Cut the occasional double-entry that still creeps in, so data flows between sales, stock, and accounting automatically.

opts.t: Often — it’s part of the daily routine

opp.text: Eliminate daily re-keying — enter information once and let it flow across quotes, invoices, inventory, and accounts.

opts.t: Constantly — double and triple entry is normal

opp.text: Reclaim the hours lost to constant re-entry — one connected system means data is captured once, used everywhere.

q: Do things slip through the cracks — late invoices, missed follow-ups, forgotten renewals?

opp.text: Stop the occasional missed invoice or follow-up with automated reminders, so revenue doesn’t quietly leak.

opts.t: Yes, regularly — we chase our tail

opp.text: Plug the leaks: automatic invoicing, follow-up reminders, and renewal alerts so nothing billable gets forgotten.

opts.t: Honestly, we don’t know what we miss

opp.text: Make every order, invoice, and renewal trackable — so you can see (and capture) revenue that currently slips away unseen.

q: If your business doubled next year, could your current setup handle it?

opp.text: Remove the strain points that cap your growth, so taking on more work doesn’t mean more chaos.
Build a system that grows with you — add capacity and modules as you scale, without rebuilding how you work.
Break the ceiling you’ve already hit — a real system absorbs the volume that manual processes no longer can.

q: How much of your week goes to admin instead of running the business?

opp.text: Automate the manageable-but-repetitive admin so even that time goes back into the business.

opts.t: Too much — admin eats my days

opp.text: Win back the days lost to admin — automated workflows, approvals, and reporting handle the routine for you.

opts.t: Almost all of it — I’m drowning in admin

opp.text: Get out from under the admin entirely, so your time goes to growing the business instead of running its paperwork.
